risk: Message Loss via Escalation End Event without Sender Notification
consequence: The ExclusiveGateway_80 routes non-matching order types to EndEvent_11 (Escalation End) without an alert adapter or dead-letter queue. The sender system (Glovia) will not receive an error callback because returnExceptionToSender is set to false.
mitigation: Unit tests TC_GLOVIA_003 and TC_GLOVIA_005 assert on the Escalation Code RoutingConditionNotMet. Mitigation requires adding an alert notification step or Dead Letter Queue (JMS) write before EndEvent_11.

risk: Unconnected / Floating Groovy Script Logic in Integration Process
consequence: Script CallActivity_77 (GLOVIA_Conditioncheck_Salesorder_Create.groovy) and Content Modifier CallActivity_86 are defined inside Process_1 but have no incoming or outgoing sequence flows. Valid order codes ('YORB', 'YICB', 'POR', 'MNZ', 'PLM') checked by the script are never evaluated by the active router.
mitigation: Test suite validates routing conditions directly against runtime gateway expressions. The integration architecture must be updated to either wire CallActivity_77 into the sequence flow before ExclusiveGateway_80 or remove obsolete elements.

consequence: If Glovia changes payload fields, Message Mapping CallActivity_102 (Test_Mapping.mmap) fails. Although SubProcess_91 logs the payload via Log_Payload (1).gsh, the message is unretrievable if MPL retention expires.
mitigation: TC_GLOVIA_004 validates that CallActivity_97 reads ${property.InputPayload} and logs it as an attachment, preventing loss of the inbound request body during failure diagnosis.

consequence: ParallelGateway_74 has only a single outgoing branch (SequenceFlow_109) in the BPMN XML, creating an unnecessary multicast overhead and potential race condition if additional asynchronous branches are attached in the future without join semantics.
mitigation: Test cases assert single-threaded sequential path execution from ParallelGateway_74 directly into ExclusiveGateway_80.
